content.text:
I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all four figure briefs, and traced each limitation, part, relationship, and figure element back to the disclosure.

**Ledger highlights (all traced):**

- **Claim 1 / 11 core chain** — branch limit below sum of ratings; per-channel contactor, connector current sensor, control-pilot interface, local connector identifier; upstream branch current sensor; stored authorization/requested current/minimum sustaining current/energy-deficit; subtract measured non-charging branch load and configurable safety reserve; sustaining-first then deficit distribution; pilot send plus connector-sensor verification; reduced pilot command; verification interval; one-at-a-time ordered shedding — each maps to exact disclosure wording ("subtracts measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch limit", "opens connector contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the branch limit").
- **Dependent claims 2–10, 12–16** — re-measurement between openings ("until measured branch current is below the branch limit"), three-condition reclosure, welded-contactor recording with inhibit plus local fault indicator, isolated local bus, network interface/nonvolatile memory/offline continuation, token-gated new sessions with expiry, tamper-evident meter sequence, and service-input mapping with agreement-gated storage all have affirmative disclosure passages.
- **Numerals 100–140 and 202–216** — each appears in exactly one figure role and one description role; no numeral carries two meanings; every ledger entry appears in at least one brief and in the description; the FIG. 4 shape order in the brief matches the leader assignments (upper diamond 210, rectangle-between-diamonds 212, lower diamond 214, bottom rectangle 216) and matches the described branching, including the "no welded condition" path to 216 and the terminator for the recorded condition.
- **Figure geometry** — the only shape choices (dashed enclosure, plain blocks, small square contactor, small circle sensor, rounded-rectangle vehicle) are marked "shown schematically" and carry no proportion, material, taper, depth, or contact-topology statement; substantive relationships that are verbalized — branch sensor upstream of all three drops, connector current sensor downstream of the contactor and in the path to the vehicle connector, non-charging load on the branch but off the bus, bus reaching only the two connector channels — each trace to "measures total current upstream of the connector contactors", "connector current remains above a leakage threshold after an open command", "measured non-charging branch load", and "communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus".
- **Text hygiene** — no "by way of example" shape hedges, no "any closed outline" language, no drafting notes, placeholders, open questions, or unresolved alternatives; claims and description use identical terms ("branch current limit", "last accepted branch limit" expressly defined against it; "edge controller 106, also referred to herein as a controller"); no means-plus-function; cross-reference and government-support sections match the brief's "No priority claim. No federally sponsored research".

I found no untraced technical assertion and no verified internal inconsistency, so the findings array is empty.

content.text:
I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all four figure briefs, tracing each claim limitation, numeral, and structural statement to the disclosure.

## What traced cleanly

- **Claims 1–16**: every limitation maps to an affirmative disclosure passage — branch limit below the sum of connector ratings, per-channel contactor/sensor/pilot interface/identifier, upstream branch sensor, the stored quadruple (authorization, requested current, minimum sustaining current, energy deficit), the subtract-reserve-and-non-charging-load allocation, sustaining-first then deficit distribution, pilot send plus connector verification, reduced pilot command, verification interval, ordered one-at-a-time shedding, three-condition reclosure with randomized delay, leakage-threshold welded detection with inhibit and local fault indicator, isolated local bus, network interface with signed token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory, outage behaviour, tamper-evident meter sequence, and the service-input mapping with confirm-before-store.
- **Numerals 100–140 and 202–216**: each designates one part consistently across the ledger, the four briefs, and the description; every ledger numeral appears in a figure and in the description; no orphan or double-assigned numeral.
- **FIG. 4 flow**: the eight-shape column, the two diamonds, both return paths, and the terminator match the described step sequence 202→204→206→208→210→212→214→216 exactly.
- **Formalities**: no priority claim, "Not applicable" government support, no means-plus-function, two statutory classes, abstract ≈144 words, no drafting notes or placeholders anywhere.

## What I flagged

Two related items, both concerning how the edge controller reads the per-connector current sensors — the one architectural relationship the disclosure never states.

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. Every limitation of claims 1-16 (apparatus 1-10 and method 11-16), every numeral in draft/numerals.md (100, 102, 104, 106, 108, 110, 112, 114, 116, 118, 120, 122, 124, 126, 128, 130, 140 and steps 202-216), every numbered part and structural, positional, connective and operational statement in draft/08-detailed-description.md, draft/06-summary.md, draft/07-drawings.md and draft/10-abstract.md, and every line-work statement in figures/FIG-1.md through FIG-4.md were checked one by one against affirmative USER passages in input/disclosure.md and input/conversation.md. The disclosure affirmatively supports: branch limit lower than the sum of connector ratings; per-channel contactor, connector current sensor, control-pilot interface and local connector identifier; branch current sensor upstream of the connector contactors as an independent safety input; isolated local bus to the connector interfaces and contactors; the stored charging authorization, requested current, minimum sustaining current and energy-deficit value; per-interval subtraction of measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve to obtain available charging current; sustaining-current-first assignment then deficit-based distribution of the remainder; pilot send and connector-sensor verification; reduced pilot command followed after a verification interval by one-at-a-time contactor opening in a stored shedding order until branch current is below the limit; three-condition reclosure (zero connector current, connected-vehicle pilot report, randomized recovery delay); leakage-threshold welded-contactor recording with inhibit of the other contactors on the branch and operation of a local fault indicator; network interface, signed local authorization token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory, outage continuation of already authorized sessions, refusal of new sessions absent an unexpired authorizing token, and tamper-evident meter records uploaded on return; and the service-input mapping by one low-energy pilot transition at a time with storage only after the sensed channel agrees. Numeral uniqueness, claim-to-description term agreement, antecedent basis, the FIG. 4 step sequence 202-204-206-208-210-212-214-216 against the described flow, and the absence of drafting notes, placeholders, open questions or unresolved alternatives were all verified. No section lines or cross-sections exist, so no repeated section designation is at issue. Two findings remain, both on the single relationship the sources never describe: how the edge controller is coupled to the connector current sensors. draft/08 verbalizes a dedicated "sensing connection" distinct from the isolated local bus, and figures/FIG-2.md renders that separate path, while the disclosure states only that the controller "communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus" and that it "verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor" - it never says the sensors are read over a separate path or over the bus. The same statement also puts FIG. 2 out of step with FIG. 1, whose enumerated line work gives each connector-channel block only a branch drop from above and a bus branch from below, with no per-channel sensing line to the edge controller. Fixes below neutralize the verbalized architecture to the disclosed coupling and reconcile the two briefs without adding any new structure.

findings.title: Dedicated per-connector "sensing connection" separate from the isolated local bus is not affirmatively disclosed
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, FIG. 2 paragraph; figures/FIG-2.md, fourth paragraph
findings.detail: The description asserts a specific coupling architecture: the contactor and control-pilot interface are on the isolated local bus 108, while the connector current sensor 124 is read over a separate, distinct connection. The disclosure describes the bus contents and the fact of verification, but contains no passage describing how the controller is coupled to the connector current sensors, and no passage describing a sensing connection separate from the bus. Naming a distinct connection is a connection-topology statement conveying technical substance (a dedicated sensing path versus a shared isolated bus), not a mere depiction convention. The bare coupling itself is supported, because the controller must read the sensor in order to verify; only the assertion that it is a separate named connection is untraced.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The edge controller 106 is also coupled to the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel by a sensing connection, and reads the connector current measured by the connector current sensor 124 over that connection." (draft/08) and "It is the sensing connection to the edge controller and carries no reference numeral of its own." (figures/FIG-2.md). Nearest source passages, which show the gap: "A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus." and "The controller sends each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface and verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor." (input/disclosure.md). No affirmative passage states that the connector current sensor is coupled by a connection separate from the isolated local bus, or how the controller reads that sensor.
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md replace the sentence with: "The edge controller 106 is coupled to the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel and reads the connector current measured by the connector current sensor 124." In figures/FIG-2.md replace "It is the sensing connection to the edge controller and carries no reference numeral of its own." with: "It represents the coupling by which the edge controller reads the connector current sensor and carries no reference numeral of its own." Make no other change to the line work.

findings.title: FIG. 1 and FIG. 2 disagree on the couplings reaching a connector channel
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md, blocks and bus paragraphs; figures/FIG-2.md, fourth paragraph
findings.detail: FIG. 1 enumerates the line work exhaustively and gives each connector-channel block exactly two couplings: a short vertical drop from the branch conductor to its top edge and a short vertical branch rising from the isolated local bus to its bottom edge. FIG. 2, showing the same first connector channel 120 in detail, adds a third external line leaving the channel downward from the connector current sensor toward the edge controller. As written, FIG. 1 depicts the isolated local bus as the only controller coupling to a channel, while FIG. 2 depicts an additional separate one; the two briefs cannot both be rendered faithfully without contradicting each other.
findings.evidence: FIG-1.md: "A short vertical line drops from the horizontal line to the top edge of each of the three blocks, connecting all three in parallel." and "One short vertical branch rises from this bus line to the bottom edge of the leftmost block and another to the bottom edge of the middle block." FIG-2.md: "A straight solid vertical line leaves the lower side of that circle, runs downward, crosses the lower side of the dashed rectangle and ends free a short distance beneath it."
findings.fix: Add the following sentence to figures/FIG-1.md immediately after the bus paragraph, so the enumerated line work is a level-of-detail choice rather than an assertion that the bus is the only coupling: "The couplings by which the edge controller reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels are shown in FIG. 2 and are not drawn in this figure; no additional line work is added here for them." This is renderer guidance only and adds no structure to the application text or claims.
